title: Credit only what was shown
statement: Credit only what a student showed in the mode being assessed: a written plan is not evidence of a spoken performance.
example: One lesson guards this in three places: its rubric, its instructions and its closing summary.
detail: A Grade 5 unit on performance made observed delivery the condition for credit. Its rubric says not to infer actual oral performance from typed claims, its instructions tell a student who cannot speak to rehearse silently and write a plan that shows reasoning but does not record delivery, and its closing summary says a written explanation does not by itself prove spoken delivery; a review counted these as three independent, redundant guards (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW-2026-09-08-R18.md`).

evidence.quote: "Do not infer actual oral performance from typed claims"
"Your written explanation does not by itself prove spoken delivery."
No arbitrary word or paragraph count, no fixed interpretation, and no claim to observe revision from final text alone.
The instruction to reread and revise supports the writing process; do not claim to observe private revision from the submitted text alone.
A typed plan can demonstrate reasoning. It cannot prove oral delivery or performance fluency.
A typed plan can satisfy text meaning and revision reasoning but cannot receive an observed oral-delivery score.
Typed explanations must not be reported as proof of oral delivery.
Do not claim oral delivery occurred from a typed answer.
Typed assessment fixtures do not prove a learner read the whole novel or performed aloud.
Group products need individual evidence. A solo AI conversation can rehearse a discussion but does not demonstrate collaboration with actual peers.
so on any no-microphone/typed session, the receipt still claims "out loud."
